text:
Aisha: quick RFC follow-up — proposal to split the current gateway surface into two bounded surfaces: ingest-gateway (data plane) and control-gateway (control plane). primary goals: clear ownership, smaller blast radius for changes, easier tech-debt paydown. thoughts?
Ben: high-level +1. can we keep a single public endpoint and route internally? worried about extra hop latency. what are our latency SLO implications?
Aisha: plan is to keep a single public edge for now, with an internal fanout. the split is logical at first (code/module boundary) and only physical later. target: no extra hop visible to clients for 90% of requests.
Carmen: sounds sensible. + please add a dark-launch path so we can mirror traffic to new control-gateway without impacting prod. feature-flagged rollout.
Dmitri: agree on mirror. implementation idea: an adapter layer that normalizes requests to a stable protobuf v1 API then fans out to v2 internally. reduces client churn.
Eva: integration tests will be big here. we need contract tests (consumer-driven) before any cutover. recommend adding a small contract CI job that runs nightly against staging mirror.
Frank: we also need a tech-debt backlog itemization. split the surface and then schedule focused "surgery windows" where teams can bite off 1-2 debt items. otherwise it becomes diff-and-forget.
Aisha: proposed migration steps (short):
1) introduce adapter module in current gateway (no behavior changes)
2) add feature-flagged mirror to control-gateway for control-only flows
3) run 2 weeks mirror, collect diffs + metrics
4) enable canary for selected routes (5% traffic)
5) full cutover with fallback to adapter shim
we should land step 1 in a small PR.
Ben: for step 1, can we keep hot-path in C++ runtime and spin off thin control handlers in Go? avoids runtime regressions while allowing rapid iteration.
Dmitri: yep. thin Go control service talking to runtime via gRPC. define a small stable RPC surface: GetSession, UpdateRoute, IngestChunk. keep messages explicit with versioned fields.
Carmen: example shim mapping we can use in the adapter: 
```
POST /v1/generate -> proxy to internal /v2/process
map: {"prompt":"text"} -> {"inputs":[{"role":"user","text":"text"}], "meta":{...}}
```
This lets us evolve internal message shapes without breaking public contract.
Eva: also add synthetic test harness that runs sample prompts through both paths and asserts token parity + latency within threshold. nightly diff job can surface regression alerts.
Frank: decision tradeoff: we delay some immediate debt fixes to avoid churn, but get smaller, safer changes. recommend we reserve 3 full-days per sprint for migration + debt work for first 3 sprints.
Aisha: ownership: propose infra/runtime team owns ingest-gateway, platform-api team owns control-gateway. both teams share the adapter infra. any objections?
Ben: fine, will volunteer infra for the adapter PR and canary run. @Carmen can you take the mirror instrumentation?
Carmen: yep. will add tracing spans + per-route diff histograms.
Dmitri: need to agree on metrics: request latency p50/p95, error delta, token parity rate, and cache hit-rate for KV. also track roll-forward rate for stuck sessions.
Aisha: good list. I'll draft a short RFC addendum with plan and metrics and link it here.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started: control-gateway-mirror v0.1 -> staging at 1765554499
Ben: I'll watch the canary dashboard. ping here for any regressions.
Eva: putting a note in the test plan doc for contract CI and synthetic harness. link when done.
Frank: final ask — let's make each PR <= 400 LOC if possible. keep review sizes small so we can iterate.
Aisha: agreed. thanks everyone — I'll post the addendum and break the work into tickets.
Ben: thx, good plan.
Carmen: :thumbsup:
Dmitri: :+1:
Eva: 👍
Frank: ✅
